correctness.rationale: For all q>=2,n>=3 the complete proof counts primitive two-marker necklaces by shorter gap, proves the even antipodal words must use a single orientation with disjoint first/second label sets, applies the sharp product bound floor((q-1)^2/4), and constructs matching families. All possible prefix-suffix overlaps are eliminated by the inequality n-s<=k<=t and the sole even middle-length exception; self-pairs included. Independent exhaustive clique optimization for 17 parameters, full pairwise construction checks for 84, and necklace count for 35 independently reproduce bounded cases. Finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The extremum is a complete exact all-length, all-alphabet capacity for a natural sparse synchronization code layer. It reveals a sharp parity dichotomy: necklace bound attained at all odd lengths, but even lengths have a quantified deficit forced by a balanced bipartition of nonzero labels. This structural obstruction and explicit universal construction are mathematically substantive, not a routine table or renaming.
